issue.title: sase doctor llm.model_advisory inspects only each alias pool's currently selected member, so a Contributor-model pool member is missed unless the round-robin cursor sits on it
issue.description:
Found while implementing plan `202609/muse_contributor_size_aliases.md`, which adds
`muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` to the shipped `@xsmall`, `@small`, and `@medium`
pools. Meta trains on that model's inputs and outputs, so `sase doctor -C
llm.model_advisory` is the only consent surface a user gets for that route.

**Root cause (known).** `_resolved_routes()` in
`src/sase/doctor/checks_providers_advisory.py` builds its alias routes from
`build_alias_views(overrides={})` and reads one `view.model` per alias — the pool's
_currently selected_ member, which depends on the machine-global round-robin cursor
(`~/.sase/llm_lb.json`). It never expands the pool. So a pool that contains an
advisory-flagged member is reported only while the cursor happens to sit on it.

**Desired fix.** For every alias, parse the target with `parse_model_alias_selector`
and check every member (`selector.members` plus `selector.fallback_members`), resolving
each to `(provider, model)`, so the warning is deterministic and independent of cursor
state. Keep the per-`(source, model)` de-duplication. Update the `docs/llms.md` "Model
Advisories" sentence that says the check warns "whenever one of those pools currently
selects it" once the check scans whole pools. Add a regression test that pins the
cursor away from the Muse member and still expects the WARN.

Do not change what the check treats as a route otherwise (tier mappings, launch-default
settings) and do not suppress the finding.

task_type_fields.impact:
Roughly one in four `@xsmall`/`@small`/`@medium` launches on such a machine sends the
agent's prompt, repository contents, and tool output to a model that trains on them. The
doctor check exists to make that visible, but it is silent most of the time, so a user
who runs `sase doctor` gets a false all-clear on the route that matters most.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/doctor/checks_providers_advisory.py::_resolved_routes (consumes build_alias_views, one selected member per alias)
task_type_fields.repro:
On a stock install (no user config, `muse` on PATH), at master 15763853b plus the muse
size-alias change:

1. `sase doctor -C llm.model_advisory -v` reports `OK — no configured route resolves to
   an advisory-flagged model`, even though `@xsmall`, `@small`, and `@medium` each carry
   `muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`.
2. Park the `@medium` cursor on its 4th member and rerun the check in-process, with the
   rotation state isolated so the real `llm_lb.json` is untouched:

   ```python
   import tempfile
   from pathlib import Path
   from sase.llm_provider import config as llm_config, load_balancing as lb
   lb.rotation_state_path = lambda: Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "rotation.json"
   llm_config._resolved_target_is_available = lambda _t: True
   from sase.llm_provider.config import resolve_model_alias_with_effort
   from sase.doctor.checks_providers_advisory import check_llm_model_advisory
   for _ in range(3):
       resolve_model_alias_with_effort("@medium", consume=True)
   print(check_llm_model_advisory().status)
   ```

   Fresh cursor prints `OK`; after the three consumes it prints `WARN` with
   `@medium -> muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor: Meta uses this model's inputs and outputs
   to train and improve its AI models...`. Same tree, same config, different verdict.

payload.description: The doctor check's blind spot is what makes the missing alias-pool guard material: the only consent surface for the Muse Contributor pool member fires only when the cursor sits on it.

payload.entry: Verified by the sase-14n land agent at master 87c604833. 4703e9107 makes the llm.model_advisory check expand every alias pool member and last-resort fallback, keeping per-(source, model) de-duplication, so the verdict no longer depends on the round-robin cursor. The docs/llms.md sentence now says the check warns whenever a pool includes the model, whichever member the cursor selects. tests/doctor/test_checks_providers_advisory.py pins the selected member away from the flagged one, still expects WARN, and passes.
